evidence.contract: TraitImpl describes duplicate merge errors; container parser dispatches repeatable comma-separated special trait attributes.
The locked bevy_macro_utils terminated parser invokes its item parser repeatedly and consumes comma punctuation.
For Clone, Debug, PartialEq, PartialOrd and Hash, custom form merges while ordinary form assigns Implemented directly.
Hash token generation calls the registered custom callback for Custom, while Implemented uses the type ID plus the ordinary Hash implementation.
Shared partial-reflection generation selects the stored Hash implementation and injects its tokens.
The opaque branch includes those shared generated methods.

findings.reasoning: For example, if a single reflect list supplies Hash(custom) followed by Hash, the first entry stores Custom and the second directly overwrites it with Implemented; the reversed order invokes merge on an already Implemented value and yields the explicit conflicting-registration error. Thus the duplicate order can replace an authored custom hash callback silently and can change generated code or lead to a trait-bound failure. The same assignment-versus-merge pattern is present for the other four listed traits. This is reasoning from the parser and generated-token sources, not an executed example.
findings.conditions_and_limits: Requires an enabled derive with duplicate special-trait entries and the specific order; a semantic change further requires successful expansion/compilation and relevant consumer invocation. The inspected 95e attribute declarations use ordinary, single special-trait entries; no search claims to rule out other project inputs. Whether upstream explicitly supports or rejects duplicate specifications should be confirmed with the owner.

lenses.assessment: Compiler attribute keywords and type path/name syntax are native grammar, not application magic-string classifiers; duplicate semantics are treated as a concrete parser contract.
Recorded line and field index literals are compiler metadata roles; no bespoke quantity misuse established in the inspected ranges.
ContainerAttributes and ReflectDerive own native macro metadata, while application bounded values and their validation belong to project owners.
Existing typed elapsed and fraction owners are named by current opaque wrapper declarations; parser metadata must not be mistaken for their validation.
TraitImpl distinguishes absent, native and custom implementations, but plain parser assignments bypass the same merge authority used by custom forms.
The special trait parser mutates metadata in order; a plain duplicate can replace a custom selection. Actual product invocation and runtime consequences remain conditional.
Opaque selection and registration metadata are correlated, yet no field-visibility result alone proves a whole-value application invariant.
Opaque early return avoids structural field collection, while constructors, native projection and Deserialize admission require separate actual owner evidence.
TraitImpl is already a three-case payload enum; wrapping native framework mode flags in application enums is not established as a repair.
Parsed trait state and metadata registration represent distinct stages, but conflict handling is split between merge and direct assignment for special traits.
Future correction must preserve legitimate custom callbacks, opaque wrapper setting, explicit no-auto and from-reflect options, and intended current type identity.
Reflect attributes feed parsed ContainerAttributes, ReflectDerive choice and native generated metadata. Project feature resolution, expansion and consumers remain open.
Native derives supply boilerplate, but custom clone, checked owner deserialization and opaque mode have semantic roles; no automatic removal of those settings follows.
